Senses.Explanation: This is one counted unit of wording: a sentence, phrase, clause, line, or saying. Chan records make that ordinary unit a compact object of public testing and house vocabulary: it can be requested, answered, withheld, penetrated, ranked, capped, or challenged, without making every phrase mean the same thing. An unnamed monk asks Linji Yixuan for his first, second, and third phrases; Linji separately says that one phrase must contain three mysterious gates, each with three essentials, authority, and function. Fenyang Shanzhao says that one phrase plainly encompasses the myriad forms. Yuanwu Keqin says that penetrating one phrase penetrates a thousand and ten thousand at once, then quotes Yongjia Xuanjue's line that one phrase clearly understood surpasses a hundred billion. Fada contrasts three thousand recited scripture sections with “one phrase of Caoxi,” while Pang Yun says that even one phrase is unnecessary in an exchange. Mazu Daoyi asks for a silent phrase, Yulin Tongxiu calls a conforming phrase a donkey-tethering stake for ten thousand kalpas, and Yaoshan Weiyan says he has a phrase he has never told anyone. Muchen Daomin demands an out-of-pattern phrase; Ying'an Tanhua asks how to voice a ceremonial house phrase. The longer final, upward, out-of-pattern, and conforming expressions are qualified members of this family, not new senses of the ordinary countable unit; independently lexicalized longer terms retain their own entries.
Senses.Note: Allowlist count: 15,708 occurrences in 419 texts. Family checks covered “first phrase” (第一句), “second phrase” (第二句), “third phrase” (第三句), “final phrase” (末後一句) and its shorter form (末後句), “upward phrase” (向上一句), “out-of-pattern phrase” (出格一句), the diminutive “one phrase” (一句子), “one conforming phrase” (一句合頭語), “under one phrase” (一句下), “a thousand and ten thousand phrases” (千句萬句), and the general “phrase” entry (句). Item-8 review found position and qualification families, not different objects: verse line, spoken phrase, quoted saying, and section-qualified phrase remain countable units of wording in the harvested passages. Thirteen exact-headword occurrences and three explicitly marked family occurrences replace the former thin set; two former KWICs that contained only the shorter “final phrase” form (末後句), rather than the exact headword “one phrase” (一句), were removed. Targeted searches for putative work-title forms “Collection of One Phrase” and “Book of One Phrase” returned zero, so the corpus does not license a title sense. No occurrence is retained merely to support an interpretive meaning for an unspecified phrase.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧問：「如何是第一句？」師云：「三要印開朱點側，未容擬議主賓分。」問：「如何是第二句？」師云：「妙解豈容無著問，漚和爭負截流機。」問：「如何是第三句？」師云：「看取棚頭弄傀儡，抽牽都來裏有人。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Linji Huizhao of Zhenzhou (鎮州臨濟慧照禪師語錄): the record does not name the monk who asks for the first, second, and third phrases; Linji Yixuan is the named respondent. All six attribution rungs leave the questioning monk unnamed.

Occurrences.Kwic: 一句語須具三玄門，一玄門須具三要，有權、有用。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Linji Huizhao of Zhenzhou (鎮州臨濟慧照禪師語錄), spoken by Linji Yixuan: Linji states that one phrase must contain three mysterious gates, each with three essentials, authority, and function.

Occurrences.Kwic: 參得一句透。千句萬句一時透。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Blue Cliff Record (佛果圜悟禪師碧巖錄), commentary by Yuanwu Keqin: Yuanwu says that penetrating one phrase penetrates a thousand and ten thousand phrases at once.

Occurrences.Kwic: 粉骨碎身未足酬。一句了然超百億。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Blue Cliff Record (佛果圜悟禪師碧巖錄): Yuanwu Keqin quotes a verse by Yongjia Xuanjue saying that pulverizing body and bones is insufficient repayment and that one phrase clearly understood surpasses a hundred billion. Parallel records explicitly introduce the line as Yongjia Xuanjue's.

Occurrences.Kwic: 經誦三千部。曹谿一句亡。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元), section on Fada: Fada speaks the verse contrasting three thousand recited scripture sections with their vanishing before one phrase of Caoxi.
Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元), section on Furong Taiyu: Pang Yun is the marked speaker (士曰) who says that not even one phrase is needed in his exchange with Furong Taiyu.

Occurrences.Kwic: 悄然一句作麼生。師乃近前三步。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Jingde Record of the Transmission of the Lamp (景德傳燈錄), section on Shijiu: Mazu Daoyi asks how the silent phrase is; Shijiu answers by stepping forward three paces. The headword belongs to Mazu's question.

Occurrences.Kwic: 一句合頭語萬劫繫驢橛
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of National Teacher Yulin (普濟玉琳國師語錄), small inquiry by Yulin Tongxiu: after raising Nanquan's ox case, Yulin comments that one conforming phrase is a donkey-tethering stake for ten thousand kalpas.

Occurrences.Kwic: 我有一句子，未曾向人說。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Anthology of the Patriarchal Hall (祖堂集), Yaoshan Weiyan section: Yaoshan says that he has one phrase he has never told anyone; Daowu Yuanzhi immediately answers him.

Occurrences.Kwic: 一句明明該萬象。重陽九日菊花新。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Supplement to the Transmission of the Lamp (續傳燈錄), section on Fenyang Shanzhao: Fenyang speaks the verse saying that one phrase plainly encompasses the myriad forms and that the Double-Ninth chrysanthemum is fresh.

Occurrences.Kwic: 作麼生道得出格一句？良久，喝一喝
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Compilation of Raised Old Cases in the Chan Gate (宗門拈古彙集), explicitly introduced as Tiantong Muchen Daomin's comment (天童忞云): Muchen asks the assembly to produce an out-of-pattern phrase, pauses, and shouts once.

Occurrences.Kwic: 且道報恩一句作麼生道？一爐沉水一聲佛
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Record of Guidelines by Successive Patriarchs (列祖提綱錄), imperial-birthday hall address explicitly assigned to Ying'an Tanhua (應庵華禪師): Ying'an asks how the gratitude-repaying phrase is voiced and supplies the capping line.

Occurrences.Kwic: 祖師有末後一句，吞栗棘蓬，跳金剛圈。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Record of Guidelines by Successive Patriarchs (列祖提綱錄), return-to-monastic-robes address explicitly assigned to Yuanwu Keqin: Yuanwu says that the patriarchs have a final phrase, followed by swallowing the thorny chestnut burr and leaping the diamond ring.

Occurrences.Kwic: 向上一句作麼生論量？常憶江南三月裏，鷓鴣啼處百花香。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Record of Guidelines by Successive Patriarchs (列祖提綱錄), water-and-land assembly address in which Chushi Fanqi identifies himself by name: Chushi asks how the upward phrase can be assessed and answers with a remembered Jiangnan spring scene.

Occurrences.Kwic: 直饒一句下承當得，猶是瞌睡漢。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Record of Guidelines by Successive Patriarchs (列祖提綱錄), hall address explicitly assigned to Yunmen Wenyan: Yunmen says that even someone who accepts it under one phrase is still a dozing fellow.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧到巖頭舉似頭。頭云：「雪峰不會末後句。」僧請益巖頭。頭云：「雪峰與我同條生，不與我同條死。要識末後句，只者是。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Abridged Collection of Chan Master Gutting's Recorded Sayings (古庭禪師語錄輯略), which raises the traveling Deshan-Yantou case: Yantou Quanhuo says that Xuefeng does not understand the final phrase and then says, ‘If you want to know the final phrase, it is just this.’
